profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Nashville - Brentwood) is located at 7100 Commerce Way Suite 25, Brentwood, TN 37027. The operator publishes a footprint of 19150 square feet and 1.49 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HIPAA, ISO 27001, SSAE 18. Tennessee has about 60 data centers statewide, and Greater Nashville hosts more than a third of them, with about 13 facilities operational or under construction in the Nashville metro itself, plus a separate cluster of seven data centers, mostly operated by Meta, around Gallatin roughly 30 miles northeast, per WPLN's November 2025 reporting. Franklin, Brentwood, Berry Hill, and Murfreesboro each hold a handful of additional data center facilities beyond Nashville proper. Cushman & Wakefield's market analysis, cited in that reporting, describes power availability as the top site-selection factor for developers in the region, pointing to Tennessee Valley Authority's established power infrastructure, proximity to the Cumberland River for cooling, and Nashville's status as an "emerging market" positioned alongside Austin as a newer data-center hub distinct from established markets like Phoenix, Dallas, and Atlanta.

TVA, which supplies power across the Nashville region, said in 2026 that data center demand had climbed to 18% of its industrial load in 2025 and was projected to double regionally by 2030, prompting what CEO Don Moul called the largest capital program in TVA's history: 6.2 gigawatts of new generation, more than 3.7 gigawatts of it already under construction, including a 1.5-gigawatt gas plant at Cumberland City due online later in 2026, a 1.5-gigawatt gas complex near Kingston slated for 2027, a license extension through the mid-2050s for the 4-gigawatt Browns Ferry nuclear plant approved in December 2025, and a $400 million federal grant toward small modular reactors at the Clinch River site near Oak Ridge. TVA's service territory saw more than $6.6 billion in announced capital investment in fiscal 2025, per Utility Dive's reporting, with data centers cited as the dominant driver alongside population growth.

reading.body:
Flexential Nashville—Brentwood publishes 1.49 MW of critical load UPS capacity across 19,150 square feet in Brentwood, Tennessee. At this scale, it ranks third among Tennessee's four facilities with published power specifications and represents 12 percent of the state's disclosed 12.13 MW total.

This facility is enterprise colocation, not AI infrastructure. At 1.49 MW, it cannot support model training clusters or large-scale inference deployments, which require tens to hundreds of megawatts in single facilities. Its compliance certifications—PCI DSS, SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001—suit regulated workloads like healthcare and payments, not compute-intensive AI.

Tennessee has 24 mapped data center facilities overall, but most publish no power figures. This data captures only a fraction of the state's actual data center capacity, so conclusions about regional AI readiness cannot be drawn from it. For an operator allocating compute, this site matters only if edge processing or compliance-sensitive inference justifies its smaller footprint and specialized certifications.
